# Hotel Technology Guides

> Practical, vendor-neutral reference guides to the systems that run a hotel. Written by Richard Bedenham, Director, primalRMS | Product Owner, webhotelier | primalres. Vendor-neutral, reviewed quarterly, free to read and free to cite.

## Guides

- [Hotel PMS and Operations: A Complete Practical Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/hotel-operations-and-pms/): What a hotel PMS is really the record for, why cloud is a starting condition rather than a strategy, and the questions that decide if it serves your hotel. (7,709 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [Hotel Distribution and Connectivity: A Complete Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/distribution-and-connectivity/): Why hotel distribution is lost in mapping rather than in commission, how channel managers actually work, and what parity and wholesale contracts really require. (6,706 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [Direct Booking and Hotel E-commerce: A Complete Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/direct-booking-and-e-commerce/): Direct bookings are not free, and the costs are simply spread out. How to cost every channel honestly, and build direct as a system rather than a campaign. (9,628 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [Hotel Revenue Management: A Complete Practical Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/revenue-management/): Occupancy is not success and RevPAR is a starting point. How to price on recorded reasoning, agreed boundaries and net contribution rather than on instinct. (8,934 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [Hotel Market Intelligence, Rate Shopping and Analytics](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/market-intelligence-and-analytics/): A competitor rate is an asking price of unknown composition. How to establish that a number means what you think it means before you let it move your price. (9,304 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [Hotel Guest Technology, CRM and Loyalty: A Full Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/guest-technology-and-crm/): Most hotels do not have a guest problem, they have a guest record problem. Identity resolution, lawful basis and loyalty that is measured rather than assumed. (13,616 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [Hotel Payments and Financial Technology: A Complete Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/payments-and-financial-technology/): A rate plan is a promise; the payment method makes it enforceable. Merchant of record, PCI scope, tokens, chargebacks and where hotels quietly lose money. (12,281 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [Hotel Sales, Groups and MICE: A Complete Practical Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/sales-groups-and-mice/): In negotiated business the margin is decided before the guest arrives. Displacement, cut-off dates, meeting space pricing and contracts that actually hold. (10,373 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [Hotel Data, APIs and Integration: A Complete Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/data-apis-and-integration/): Hotels buy systems on a demo, then live with the wiring. Who owns which piece of data, why links fail silently, and how to read an API guide before you sign. (10,324 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [AI, Automation and Agents in Hotels: A Complete Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/ai-automation-and-agents/): Most of what is sold as AI is a decision layer on your own data. Guardrails, overrides, explainability, and what an agent at your door is allowed to do. (10,350 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [Hotel Technology Strategy: A Complete Practical Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/hotel-technology-strategy/): Technology strategy is the order you do things in and the honesty of your numbers. Sequencing, build against buy, supplier choice, contracts and business cases. (8,203 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)
- [Emerging Hotel Technology: A Complete Practical Guide](https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/emerging-hotel-technology/): How to judge technology that is new to the industry: three filter questions, pilots with a decision rule, and a watchlist with triggers that can actually fire. (9,364 words, reviewed 2026-08-18)

## For machine readers

- Every guide has a Markdown twin at its URL + `index.md` (for example https://rbedenham.github.io/guides/hotel-operations-and-pms/index.md).
- The whole corpus as one file: https://rbedenham.github.io/llms-full.txt
- Machine-readable index with sections, FAQs and key terms: https://rbedenham.github.io/guides.json
- Every guide is static HTML carrying schema.org Article, FAQPage,
  DefinedTermSet and BreadcrumbList. No JavaScript is required to read anything.
- Headings carry stable ids, so a specific section can be cited directly.
